title: Sessions-aware active-active edge failover and graceful streaming cutover
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Hosted API traffic needs to be served active-active across regions to meet SLOs during regional degradation, yet current gateway failover indiscriminately drops in-flight streaming sessions and loses session affinity. This causes client-visible stream resets, high retry traffic, and cascading load on healthy regions. We need a sessions-aware active-active failover design that minimizes user-visible interruptions, preserves ordering for stream sessions where possible, and integrates circuit breakers + load-shedding to protect healthy regions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Region failover can be executed without forcing 90%+ of long-lived streams to reconnect; at least 75% of resumable streams must continue without full client-side backoff.
2) Rolling traffic shift plan can move traffic in 5% increments with automated rollback on SLO degradation (p95 latency > previous baseline by 20% or error rate > 0.5%).
3) Circuit breaker rules are in place per-region and per-route: open when 5xx > 1% for 5m or 10s p95 latency increase > 30%.
4) Load-shedding policy drops best-effort, non-critical requests before user-facing streaming/control-plane requests and preserves quota for high-priority customers as configured by routing policy.

5) Observability: dashboards show active_sessions_per_region, streaming_resume_rate, region_failover_count, and per-region SLOs. Alerts trigger on failover and on streaming resume failures exceeding 10% in a 10m window.
6) Runbook entries for manual failover and rollback validated in canary chaos test and included in runbook_summary.
design_notes: Overview: Implement a sessions-aware proxy layer in the edge gateway that tracks session metadata (session_id, resume_token, preferred_region) and supports soft-handoff instead of hard cutover for resumable streams.

Session types: classify sessions into: short RPC, long-polling, resumable streaming (resume tokens supported by model runtime), and non-resumable streaming. Only resumable sessions will be candidates for seamless cross-region handoff.

Sticky routing: keep initial session affinity using a session table with TTL. When a region degrades, mark preferred_region for those sessions and attempt resume via control-plane coordination to an alternate region.

Streaming resume protocol: require a resume_token issued by the serving runtime on session start; token encodes model version, last-acknowledged token position, and a signed region-hint. Gateway will attempt transparent resume with exponential backoff and jitter; if resume fails, fallback to client reconnect with explanatory error for SDKs.

Circuit breakers: per-region, per-route circuit breakers implemented at the gateway with adaptive thresholds. Breaker state exported to control plane and used to drive automated traffic shifts and to inform routing decisions.

Load shedding: classify traffic by priority (control-plane/query-critical/high, best-effort/low). During overload, shed best-effort first using probabilistic token-drop and 429 responses with Retry-After and a reason code so SDKs can backoff intelligently.

Compatibility: maintain API compatibility for non-resumable clients; these sessions will be drained with a grace period and sent a protocol-level hint to reconnect to a healthy region with client-side resume where supported.
Security: resume tokens are short-lived JWTs signed with KMS keys; tokens do not contain PII. Use existing KMS integration and rotate keys per current rotation policy.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flag + small canary (runtime-1.25): Deploy sessions-aware proxy and resume-token plumbing behind a kill-switch. Canary in us-west-2 with 1% of traffic, internal test clients only.
Phase 1 - Controlled canary: Expand to 5% public traffic in two additional regions. Run synthetic long-lived stream tests and monitor streaming_resume_rate and p95 latency.

Phase 2 - Incremental traffic shift for failover exercise: Run an orchestrated region kill in staging and then in a single production region during low traffic window; shift 10%->50%->100% via automation with 15m observation windows and automated rollback criteria.
Phase 3 - Global rollout: Enable for all regions and enable adaptive circuit-breaker-driven automatic shifts. Flag defaults to on after 3 successful exercise windows.

Rollback criteria: if in any phase p95 latency increases >20% or streaming_resume_failure_rate exceeds 10% for two consecutive observation windows, automatically revert traffic to pre-flag baseline and open incident.
testing_plan: Unit/Integration: Tests for resume token parsing, validation, and signature checks; simulated resume flows across region boundaries in CI.
E2E: Synthetic clients that open N long-lived streaming sessions (mix of resumable and non-resumable) and validate continuity after simulated region failure.
Chaos: Use failure-injection to kill region gateway instances and inter-region networking; verify automated shift, streaming resume rates, and absence of cascading retries.
Load: Bench test load-shedding behavior under token-heavy workloads to ensure non-critical drops reduce CPU and token usage on target regions.
SLO validation: Run canary monitors that emulate representative traffic and assert SLOs (availability and p95 latency) and resume-success metrics before each rollout step.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: region.active_sessions, region.streaming_resume_success_rate, region.streaming_resume_failure_rate, region.latency_p50/p95, region.5xx_rate, region.circuit_breaker_state, region.shed_rate_by_priority.
Dashboards: streaming failover overview, per-region SLO health, per-route breaker status, and customer-impacting sessions list (obfuscated identifiers).
Alerts: Pager alert if streaming_resume_failure_rate > 10% in 10m or if circuit_breaker enters OPEN state for >5m in multiple regions; Warnings if p95 latency increases >15% for 15m.
Audit logs: record each session handoff attempt and result, including resume_token validation outcome and chosen target region. Logs must be retained per compliance policy for 90 days.
Tracing: attach correlation_id for each session resume attempt to enable end-to-end investigation across gateway and runtime.
runbook_summary: Detect: Runbook is triggered by alert 'StreamingResumeFailureHigh' or 'RegionCircuitBreakerOpen'.
Assess: Confirm source region health via region.slo and infra monitors, check network path metrics and cloud provider incident feeds.

Mitigate: If partial region degradation: increase weight on healthy regions by automation; if major outage: force failover using orchestrated traffic shift automation. For streaming sessions, prioritize resume attempts for sessions with high priority flag and notify affected customers via status page.
Rollback: Use automation to revert to previous traffic weights and disable sessions-aware flag if rollback criteria met. Notify on-call and PM.
Post-incident: Run postmortem checklist, capture streaming_resume_failure patterns, and schedule follow-up fixes.
